name: Kilindi Zanzibar
neighborhood: Kendwa · the north end, in 50 acres of garden
recognition: Commissioned as a private residence for Benny Andersson of ABBA; now Elewana Kilindi Zanzibar
what_to_order: Whatever the boat landed · Swahili coconut curry · Sundowner at the waterfall bar
price_range: Resort rates only — dining included in the stay; no published à la carte
reservation: Residents only in practice — email ahead if you are not staying
best_time: Late afternoon into sunset — the domes take the western light
notes: This is the north end of Kendwa's sand; the walk from Kendwa Rocks takes about 20 minutes at low water.
verdict: Go for the room and the quiet, not for the plate — the architecture is the reason and it is a real one.
caveat: Adults-only in practice and priced accordingly; not a walk-in dining room. Confirm dining access before you arrive if you are not a resident.

name: Zuri Zanzibar — Upendo
neighborhood: Kendwa · thirteen hectares behind the sand
recognition: World's first gold EarthCheck certification for sustainable design; listed in the MICHELIN Guide hotel selection
what_to_order: Maisha's chef's set menu · Upendo's live cooking line · Sugar-cane cocktails at Bahari · Spice-garden plates
price_range: Resort dining, upper band — half board included in most rates
reservation: Book ahead for non-residents, especially for Maisha's set dinner
best_time: Bahari Grill from about 17:00 for the western light; Maisha after dark
notes: Three restaurants plus Peponi Bar and a semi-private Dhow Bar for suite and villa guests only.
verdict: The best-run kitchen group on this stretch of sand, and the only one whose sustainability claim carries an audited certificate rather than a laminated card.
caveat: Non-residents are welcome but should book; this is resort pricing and the walk in from the village road is longer than it looks on a map.

name: Nungwi fish market & the evening grills
neighborhood: Nungwi · the working beach, north of the hotel line
recognition: Working artisanal fish landing and evening grill market, Nungwi village
what_to_order: Whole grilled kingfish (nguru) · Pweza wa kuchoma · Grilled squid (ngisi) · Kachumbari
price_range: A few thousand TZS a head to eat well — the cheapest good meal on this coast
best_time: 06:00–08:00 for the landing and the auction · from 18:00 for the grills
notes: This is a Muslim working village: dress covered walking to and from the market, and expect the grills to shift entirely to after sunset during Ramadan.
verdict: The best value and the truest plate on the north tip — and the one place here where the tourist and the fisherman are eating the same fish at the same fire.
caveat: Cash only, no menu, no receipt, and prices are negotiated: settle the price per kilogram before the fish is put on the coals or you will pay a stranger's rate. Hygiene is a working beach's hygiene — go when it is busy and the turnover is fast.

name: Gold Zanzibar Beach House & Spa
neighborhood: Kendwa · on the sand, south end
what_to_order: Grilled catch of the day · Coconut-and-spice curry · Sundowner on the sand
notes: Half board is the norm; non-residents should call ahead.
verdict: Book it for the position and the service; the kitchen is competent resort cooking, not a destination in itself.
caveat: Resort pricing, and the beach in front is public — the hawker traffic does not stop at the property line.

name: Hotel Riu Palace Zanzibar
neighborhood: Between Kendwa and Nungwi · Kendwa Road
what_to_order: Buffet and three themed rooms · Sunshine Pool Bar
notes: Adults-only policy.
verdict: Reliable and entirely sealed off; the island does not get in and you do not get out. Judge it on that.
caveat: Guests only. All-inclusive wristband economics mean the village kitchens see none of this money.

name: The Z Hotel Zanzibar
neighborhood: Nungwi · on the beach, west side
what_to_order: Fresh seafood, west-facing deck · Cocktail list
notes: Sexy Fish is the hotel's own restaurant — same gate.
verdict: The most consistent non-resort kitchen on the north tip, and the only one here with a real cocktail programme.
caveat: Small property; the good tables go early in high season.

name: Essque Zalu Zanzibar — The Jetty
neighborhood: Nungwi · east side, away from the strip
what_to_order: Seafood on the jetty · Long lunch out of the wind
best_time: Lunch, or dinner on a bright moon
notes: A different bay from the Nungwi strip — check the walk.
verdict: Come for the position and the silence; the food is competent resort cooking and the jetty is the event.
caveat: The east side loses the sunset — this is a lunch and a moonlight address, not a sundowner one.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Resort Zanzibar — Nungwi
neighborhood: Nungwi · village edge
what_to_order: Buffet · Pool bar
notes: Use it as a landmark for the village walk.
verdict: Predictable. Its best feature is how close it is to better food.
caveat: Nothing here is of this island in particular.

name: Bistro' del M@r
neighborhood: Kendwa · Kendwa Road, behind the sand
what_to_order: Wood-fired pizza · Seafood pasta · Espresso
price_range: Mid — well below the beach-front rate
notes: Kendwa Road runs behind the resort line; a torch is worth having after dark.
verdict: The best-value proper Italian cooking in Kendwa, and the correct answer to a fourth consecutive night of grilled fish.
caveat: On the road, not the beach — no view, and that is the trade you are making.

name: La Fontana Restaurant & Bungalows
neighborhood: Kendwa · Kendwa Road
what_to_order: Pizza · Grilled seafood
notes: Bungalows attached if you want to stay on the road side.
verdict: Consistent rather than exciting; the safe Italian bet when the wood oven at Bistro' is full.
caveat: Nothing here is a discovery. It does not pretend to be.

name: Mama Mia
neighborhood: Nungwi · the strip
what_to_order: Gelato, churned on site · Pizza
notes: Also does pizza; the gelato is the reason.
verdict: The best sweet thing on the north tip and the only one that required real engineering.
caveat: Flavours run out late in the day; go before the evening rush if you want the full cabinet.

name: Badolina Secret Garden
neighborhood: Nungwi · Mkunguni, inland of the strip
what_to_order: Garden-sourced Italian plates · Zanzibari-Italian crossovers
notes: Inland; take a torch and a pin.
verdict: Worth the walk when it is open; do not build an evening around it without a phone call first.
caveat: ⚠ Listed as temporarily closed by one aggregator and as trading by another as of 22 Aug 2026. Unresolved — call or message before you set out. This guide will not tell you it is open when we could not confirm it.

name: Machnoo Local Restaurant
neighborhood: Nungwi · the middle of the village, off the beach
what_to_order: Swahili tapas (five dishes) · Pilau · Coconut curry (mchuzi wa nazi) · Chapati
best_time: Lunch, or early evening before the pots run down
notes: Off the beach, in the village proper: dress covered walking here.
verdict: The most instructive plate on the north tip, and it costs a fraction of the sand.
caveat: Closed Mondays. Cash. No alcohol — this is a village kitchen in a Muslim village, and that is the deal.

name: Kivulini Garden Lodge & Restaurant
neighborhood: Nungwi · beach village, garden side
what_to_order: Mchuzi wa nazi · Pilau · Mishkaki
notes: Indian dishes on the menu too — the island's Indian layer is not decoration, it is history.
verdict: The best compromise on the north tip between the honest kitchen and the comfortable chair.
caveat: Service runs at village pace. That is not a fault, but plan around it.

name: Baraka Beach Restaurant
neighborhood: Nungwi · on the sand
what_to_order: Grilled catch · Coconut rice
notes: Bungalows attached.
verdict: Fine, cheap, and exactly where you want to be at two in the afternoon.
caveat: Beach-front variability: it is better when it is busy.

name: Langi Langi Beach Bungalows
neighborhood: Nungwi · beach village, west side
what_to_order: Seafood platter · Fish curry · Breakfast on the terrace
reservation: Worth calling for a sunset table
notes: Bungalows attached; the restaurant is open to non-residents.
verdict: The most reliable independent kitchen on Nungwi beach, and the best terrace among them.
caveat: Popular at sunset — the front tables are gone by 17:30 in high season.

name: The Fisherman Local Restaurant
neighborhood: Kendwa · off the road, behind the beach
what_to_order: Grilled lobster · Pweza wa nazi · Whole grilled fish
notes: Off the beach behind the road; ask at any dive shop for the turning.
verdict: The best price-to-plate ratio in Kendwa, full stop.
caveat: Cash, no view, and the kitchen runs out. Go early.

name: Essence Restaurant
neighborhood: Kendwa · at Amaan Kendwa, on the beach
what_to_order: Biryani · Fish curry · Tandoor plates
notes: Inside Amaan Kendwa; walk in off the sand.
verdict: The most varied menu on Kendwa beach and a real change of register from the nightly grill.
caveat: Beachfront pricing, and it is a hotel restaurant — the room is not the reason, the food is.

name: Sexy Fish
neighborhood: Nungwi · at The Z Hotel, west-facing deck
address: The Z Hotel, Nungwi, Kaskazini A
what_to_order: Sashimi and sushi · Grilled catch · Cocktails on the deck
notes: Reached through The Z Hotel.
verdict: The best cooking on the north tip that is not attached to a five-star resort — and the only serious raw-fish programme up here.
caveat: Book. Small deck, and the sunset tables are spoken for well in advance in high season.

name: Maisha Beach — Seafood & Cocktails
neighborhood: Nungwi · Aluna road, on the sand
what_to_order: Tuna poke bowl · Grilled seafood · Aubergine curry · Fresh juices and smoothies
reservation: WhatsApp for a table on Friday or Saturday
best_time: Friday and Saturday from 20:00; any evening for the sunset
notes: Booking by email, phone or WhatsApp.
verdict: The best food-to-atmosphere ratio on Nungwi sand, and the rare beach bar whose kitchen is not an afterthought.
caveat: Low season and Ramadan change the event programme — check before you plan a night around it.

name: Kendwa Rocks Beach Hotel
neighborhood: Kendwa · centre of the sand
address: Kendwa Road, Kendwa Beach, Kaskazini A
recognition: Full Moon Party running since 1996 by the venue's own account; monthly, first Saturday after the full moon
what_to_order: Grilled fish and chips off the beach kitchen · Full Moon buffet · A cold Kilimanjaro at sunset
price_range: Low-mid for food and drink; party tickets separate
reservation: Not for the bar; book rooms far ahead for full-moon weekends
best_time: Sunset any night · the first Saturday after a full moon for the event
notes: The Rocks Lounge Club runs Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday from 22:00.
verdict: Go for the night it is famous for, or go on any other night for a cheap drink on the best-positioned sand in Kendwa; do not go expecting the cooking to be the point.
caveat: On party nights this is a several-thousand-person event with a ticket and a buffet — loud, crowded and nothing like the 1996 story. If that is not what you came for, check the moon before you book the room.

name: Sunset Kendwa
neighborhood: Kendwa · next along the sand from Kendwa Rocks
address: Kendwa Road, Kendwa Beach, Kaskazini A
what_to_order: Grilled fish · Sundowner
notes: Walkable from Kendwa Rocks along the sand in two minutes.
verdict: The sane alternative fifty metres up the beach on a loud night.
caveat: Casual kitchen; manage expectations and order simply.

name: Mangi's Beach Bar & Restaurant
neighborhood: Nungwi · on the sand
what_to_order: Cold beer at sunset · Grilled fish
notes: On the beach, mid-strip.
verdict: When it is running, it is the social centre of the Nungwi sand.
caveat: ⚠ Listed as temporarily closed by one aggregator and as trading by another as of 22 Aug 2026. Walk past and look before you plan around it.

name: Cholo's Bar
neighborhood: Nungwi · on the sand, driftwood end
what_to_order: Cold beer · Konyagi and tonic
notes: Look for the driftwood; you cannot mistake it.
verdict: The one bar up here with a genuine character rather than a decorated one — and the boats are real boats.
caveat: Beach-bar standards throughout; go for the room, not the kitchen.

name: Kajibange Bar
neighborhood: Nungwi · Mkunguni, inland
what_to_order: Cold beer · Grilled skewers
notes: Guest house attached.
verdict: No view, no theatre, half the price.
caveat: Inland and unlit — take a torch and a pin.

name: Coccobello African Village
neighborhood: Between Kendwa and Nungwi · Cocobelo way
what_to_order: Simple grill · Cold drinks
notes: Useful at high tide when the sand route is gone.
verdict: Not a destination; a well-placed stop.
caveat: On the road, not the beach.

name: Waves Restaurant
neighborhood: Nungwi · on the sand
what_to_order: Grilled fish · Breakfast on the beach
notes: On the main Nungwi sand.
verdict: Consistent, well-sited, and honest about being neither more nor less.
caveat: Nothing here will surprise you.

name: Zanzibar Watersports @ Kendwa Rocks
neighborhood: Kendwa · on the beach at Kendwa Rocks
price_range: Standard Zanzibar dive rates; Mnemba carries a US$10 per-person conservation fee
notes: Based at Kendwa Rocks.
verdict: The convenient option if you are staying in Kendwa; the deep-site briefing is the thing to listen to.
caveat: Leven Bank is a strong-current, experienced-divers-only site and can only be dived on certain tides. Do not book it as your first dive of a trip.

name: Spanish Dancer Divers
neighborhood: Nungwi · on the beach
price_range: Standard rates + US$10 Mnemba conservation fee
notes: PADI 5-star dive resort.
verdict: The most experienced dive operation on the north tip, and the one to ask about conditions before you commit.
caveat: Mnemba trips carry the conservation-area fee on top of the dive price.

name: Diving Poseidon
neighborhood: Nungwi · on the beach
notes: On the Nungwi strip.
verdict: Competent and conveniently placed; compare the briefing, not the price.
caveat: Confirm the boat and the group size before paying.

name: The Nungwi dhow yards
neighborhood: Nungwi · the working beach north of the hotels
address: Nungwi beach, north of the hotel line
price_range: Free to watch; a guide expects a tip
notes: Runs into the fish market at the same end of the beach — do both in one walk.
verdict: The most alive craft on this island and the reason to walk north out of the bar strip at all.
caveat: This is a workplace. Ask before photographing; do not climb on the boats; tip the guide if you take one.

name: Mnarani Marine Turtles Conservation Pond
neighborhood: Nungwi · by the lighthouse, north-east of the village
notes: Also runs a 'Trash to Treasures' recycling project, going since June 2016.
verdict: The honest option of the two turtle ponds here: community-founded, tidally flushed, with an actual annual release rather than a website paragraph.
caveat: It is still a captive pond with paying visitors, and the animals are handled. If that is a line for you, do not go — watch for turtles on a Mnemba dive instead.

name: Baraka Natural Aquarium
neighborhood: Nungwi · Mkunguni
notes: The operator's own conservation claims are quoted above; the dispute is quoted alongside them deliberately.
verdict: Contested, and we could not settle it. If you want turtles, go to Mnarani, or dive Mnemba and see them wild.
caveat: ⚠ Animal-welfare concerns are substantial and repeated in visitor accounts. Read them before you buy a ticket.

name: Ras Nungwi Lighthouse
neighborhood: Nungwi · the northern point itself
notes: Right beside the Mnarani turtle pond — do them together.
verdict: Five minutes of your day and the best orientation on the whole cape — everything in this guide is arranged around this corner.
caveat: No public access to the tower. Sources disagree on whether the first station was 1881 or 1886.

name: Kendwa Beach
neighborhood: Kendwa · the whole west-facing sand
best_time: Low water in the late afternoon
notes: Looks out on Daloni and, beyond it, Tumbatu.
verdict: Not a matter of taste: this is a bathymetric fact and it is why you are here rather than at Paje.
caveat: Public beach — the hawker traffic is constant, and it is a Muslim island: cover up walking off the sand.

name: Mkokotoni landing & market
neighborhood: West coast · the district capital, ~20 km south of Kendwa
what_to_order: Nguru (kingfish) · Jodari (tuna) · Pweza (octopus) · Dagaa
price_range: Wholesale — bring shillings and small notes
notes: About 20 km south of Kendwa on the west-coast road.
verdict: If you cook, this is the most useful hour on the island: it is where the north's fish is actually priced.
caveat: Arrive before mid-morning or the good fish is gone. Cash only. This is a working market, not a tour stop.

name: Tumbatu Island
neighborhood: Offshore, west · the island Kendwa looks at
price_range: Guided cultural visit, arranged in advance
reservation: Permit + approved guide, arranged days ahead through Mkokotoni
best_time: Morning crossing on a settled tide
notes: Crossed from Mkokotoni. Also a dive site — the shallow Tumbatu reefs are the north's fallback when Leven Bank is unworkable.
verdict: The most historically important thing visible from Kendwa sand, and the one you are least entitled to walk into.
caveat: ⚠ Not an open destination. Anyone not from Tumbatu — including Zanzibaris — needs written permission from the village elders, and visits go with an approved local guide who asks for that blessing first. Do not hire a boat and turn up. The island's reputation for keeping outsiders out is earned and deliberate.

name: Mangapwani coral cave & slave chamber
neighborhood: West coast · about 20 km north of Stone Town
reservation: None; a guide is worth it
best_time: Morning, on the way to or from Stone Town
notes: On the west-coast road between Kendwa and Stone Town — the natural stop on that drive.
verdict: Go, and take a guide who will tell it properly. This is the counterweight to every clove-scented spice tour on the island.
caveat: Sombre, unlit and low-ceilinged. Entry around US$5 for a foreign adult; small notes. Not a place for a casual half hour between beaches.

name: Stone Town
neighborhood: South-west · about 56 km from Kendwa, roughly 1 h 15 by road
price_range: Transfer roughly US$50–70 each way by private car; shared transfers less
reservation: Arrange the car the day before
best_time: Leave Kendwa by 08:00; be at Forodhani by 18:00
notes: UNESCO World Heritage inscribed 2000.
verdict: A full day or don't bother. The drive each way eats three hours of daylight.
caveat: Do not attempt it as a half-day from Kendwa; the road is slow and you will see a car park and a curio shop.

name: Forodhani Gardens night market
neighborhood: Stone Town · the seafront, in front of the Old Fort
what_to_order: Zanzibar pizza · Urojo (Zanzibar mix) · Mishkaki · Sugar-cane juice with lime and ginger
notes: In front of the Old Fort and the House of Wonders.
verdict: Go for the things cooked in front of you and nothing else — that rule turns a tourist trap into the best street food on the island.
caveat: ⚠ Never take from a tray that has been sitting out. Agree the price before it is made — overcharging visitors is routine here. Cash, small notes.

name: Emerson Spice Rooftop Tea House
neighborhood: Stone Town · Tharia Street, Mkunazini
what_to_order: The seafood tasting menu · Sundowners on the roof · Lunch, 12:30–16:00
price_range: US$55 per person for the tasting menu, drinks extra
notes: Its sister rooftop, Emerson on Hurumzi, runs a US$45 three-course dinner at 19:00 with taarab music.
verdict: The island's best table by a distance — and the only one where the room, the hour and the cooking are all doing the same thing.
caveat: Reservation required, in advance. Check the day: the rooftop has carried scheduled closures in past seasons.

name: Emerson on Hurumzi Tea House
neighborhood: Stone Town · 236 Hurumzi Street, Kiponda
what_to_order: Three-course Swahili dinner · Taarab performance
price_range: US$45 per person, three courses, drinks extra
notes: Sister property to Emerson Spice.
verdict: Choose this one for the music and the room; choose Emerson Spice for the food.
caveat: Floor seating on rugs — not for every back. Deposit required to confirm.

name: Lukmaan Restaurant
neighborhood: Stone Town · New Mkunazini Road
what_to_order: Biryani · Urojo · Fish in coconut · Mkate wa kumimina
notes: Halal; a Ramadan-hours change is likely.
verdict: The single most educational plate on the island, and it costs almost nothing.
caveat: No alcohol, shared tables, and it empties fast at Friday lunch. Cash.

name: Darajani Market
neighborhood: Stone Town · Market Street
what_to_order: Cloves (karafuu) · Cardamom, cinnamon, nutmeg · Kahawa chungu
notes: The coffee men brew kahawa chungu on charcoal at the edges — small cups, brass kettle, no sugar.
verdict: The best provisioning stop on Unguja and the only place to buy spice at a real price.
caveat: Crowded, hot, and the fish hall is not for the squeamish. Buy spice loose by weight, never in a printed gift box — the box costs more than the cloves.

name: Mnemba Atoll
neighborhood: Offshore, north-east · reached from Nungwi or Matemwe
price_range: Dive or snorkel trip + US$10 per-person conservation fee
reservation: Through any north-tip dive centre, day before
best_time: Early departure, before the wind gets up
notes: Around 1 h 15 by road from Kendwa to the Matemwe launch, or by boat from Nungwi.
verdict: The place to see turtles honestly — wild, unfed and not in a pond.
caveat: ⚠ You cannot land on the island: it is private, and boats that promise a beach landing are selling you something they cannot deliver. The US$10 conservation fee is on top of the trip price.

name: Leven Bank
neighborhood: Offshore, north · the Pemba Channel
reservation: Book on a tide, not on a date
notes: Run from both Kendwa and Nungwi.
verdict: The best dive reachable from this beach, and the one most likely to be cancelled — take the cancellation as professionalism, not bad luck.
caveat: ⚠ Experienced divers only, strong current, and genuinely tide-gated. Do not make it your first dive of a trip. The name most likely honours HMS Leven, which surveyed this coast in the 1820s — but we could not confirm the naming from a primary source, so we are not asserting it.

name: Kizimbani spice plantation
neighborhood: Central Unguja · inland from Stone Town, on the Kendwa road
what_to_order: Clove (karafuu) · Nutmeg and mace · Vanilla · Cinnamon bark and leaf
notes: A natural stop on the Kendwa–Stone Town road.
verdict: The right spice farm if you actually cook — you leave knowing what an unopened flower bud smells like, which no jar will teach you.
caveat: Every driver has a spice farm they are paid to take you to. Name Kizimbani and hold to it. Harvest activity peaks in the dry seasons — June to October and December to February.

name: The Old Fort (Ngome Kongwe)
neighborhood: Stone Town · seafront, beside Forodhani
notes: Directly beside the Forodhani gardens.
verdict: Twenty minutes, free, and it orients the whole seafront.
caveat: The stalls inside are curio stalls; the building is the point.

name: Christ Church Cathedral & the slave-market memorial
neighborhood: Stone Town · Mkunazini
notes: A few minutes' walk from Lukmaan.
verdict: Non-optional if you are going to enjoy the cloves.
caveat: Entry fee; the chambers are low, dark and deliberately hard.

name: House of Wonders (Beit el-Ajaib)
neighborhood: Stone Town · seafront
notes: Beside the Old Fort and Forodhani.
verdict: Closed, and worth walking past anyway: it is the physical state of this island's maritime memory.
caveat: ⚠ Closed to the public. Anyone offering you a tour inside is not selling what they say they are.

name: Freddie Mercury House
neighborhood: Stone Town · Kenyatta Road, Shangani
notes: In Shangani, near the seafront.
verdict: Twenty minutes and a small fee; go for the migration story, not the memorabilia.
caveat: Small, and priced as a novelty. Do not build a morning around it.

name: Smiles Beach Hotel
neighborhood: Nungwi · Mkunguni side
notes: Non-residents welcome.
verdict: A calm table when the strip is not.
caveat: Limited menu out of season.

name: Flame Tree Cottages
neighborhood: Nungwi · garden side, off the strip
notes: Garden setting.
verdict: Pleasant and quiet; a shade address rather than a food one.
caveat: Off the beach — no view.

name: Nungwi village shops & the provisioning line
neighborhood: Nungwi · inland of the beach
notes: For bulk spice, cheese, wine and anything imported: Darajani and the Stone Town supermarkets.
verdict: Perfectly adequate for cooking simply and completely inadequate for cooking Europeanly. Plan accordingly.
caveat: ⚠ Cold chain is the constraint: buy fish at the landing and cook it the same day. Cash, small notes. Friday around midday the village closes for prayers.
